nodes.title: Skepticism Is Suspension, Not Cynicism
nodes.statement: Skepticism is an active suspension of disposition — a state of neutrality which eschews religious, biased rational, social narrative-based, or dogmatic dispositions when encountering new observations, ideas, and data. It is not cynicism, doubt, or reflexive dismissal.

nodes.title: Challenge Narrative, Not Novelty
nodes.statement: It is Narrative, not novelty, which demands our skepticism. The first duty of ethical skepticism is to detect and oppose agency, not merely bias. Agency may turn out to be correct, but that is for evidence to determine, not assumption.

nodes.title: Ignorance Is a Verb
nodes.statement: Ignorance is an action cultivated through enforcement or neglect, not a passive state of being. The purpose of misrepresentation is to cultivate ignorance — not irrationality — because ignorance is harder to self-sense and more difficult to dispel.

nodes.title: Not Wrong ≠ Correct
nodes.statement: If someone cannot prove you wrong, they cannot claim to be correct. To assume that because one cannot be disproven, one is therefore correct, is fallacious via the Argument from Ignorance. Absence of evidence is not evidence of absence.

nodes.title: The Null Hypothesis Discipline
nodes.statement: Every claim is tested against the null (status quo). The process: establish claim P, establish null N, define necessary observables, gather evidence (facts, patterns, stories), apply falsification, determine outcome. Retain N, Accept P, Accept P and Reject N, or remain Undecided.

nodes.title: The Epistemic Journey (Certainty → Uncertainty → Exploration)
nodes.statement: Effective inquiry requires consciously transitioning from comfortable certainty into productive uncertainty. True mastery emerges from courageously embracing exploration — engaging the unknown and transforming uncertainty into discovery.

nodes.title: The Four Stages of Reasoning (PSCPR)
nodes.statement: Observation (known knowns) → Analysis (known unknowns) → Inference (unknown knowns) → Exploration (unknown unknowns). Each stage corresponds to a type of expert (T1 → T1 → T2 → T3).

nodes.title: The Three Modes of Inference
nodes.statement: Deduction (what is true — facts), Induction (what usually happens — patterns), Abduction (what possibly happens — stories). Valid deductive forms: Modus Ponens, Modus Tollens. Invalid: Affirming the Consequent, Denying the Antecedent. Stories are to be tested, not believed.

nodes.title: Truth as a Stable Attractor
nodes.statement: Truth behaves like a stable attractor in the space of reasoning. Valid inference (MP, MT) functions as negative feedback — convergent. Invalid inference (DA, AC) functions as positive feedback — divergent. Circular reasoning is a neutral orbit.

nodes.title: The Epistemological Posture
nodes.statement: Epistemic humility (willingness to be wrong), deontological doubt (moral duty to avoid false positives), ontological confidence (reality has structure that can be probed). Seek truth through coherence and invariance. Prefer a non-answer to a confidently false answer.

nodes.title: The Art of the Question
nodes.statement: The prosecutorial deductive critical path of reasoning and questioning leads to the most informative discoveries. The quality of questions matters more than the speed of answers. Better questions provoke rare results that change the status quo.

nodes.title: Informative Error Over Hollow Correctness
nodes.statement: Wrong answers to proper questions are informative; right answers to wrong questions masquerade like naked emperors. Error is acceptable; fragility is not. Don't fear being wrong — fear not being informative.

nodes.title: The Tree of Knowledge Obfuscation
nodes.statement: Be aware of crooked arguing, skilled lying, coercion, irrelevance, smoke & mirrors, inference tricks, narrative manipulation, and agency-driven thinking. The TOKO taxonomy (see [METHODOLOGY.md](METHODOLOGY.md) §4) operationalizes detection of these patterns.

nodes.title: Information Reliability Over Probative Value
nodes.statement: Prioritize increasing the reliability of information over attempting to increase the probative nature of already-reliable data. Reduce uncertainty before seeking new data. Validate assumptions before building on them. Falsify alternatives before adopting positions.

nodes.title: The Selected Axioms of The Ethical Skeptic
nodes.statement: (1st) Accurate is simple, but simple is not therefore accurate. (3rd) If it is simple, everyone understands it, most believe it, but it still cannot be tested — it is most likely wrong. (4th) When human intervention is the critical feature of a hypothesis, human intervention to obfuscate that hypothesis forces it into becoming the null. (7th) Once plurality is introduced under Ockham's Razor, it cannot be dismissed by skepticism alone. (10th/Hempel's Narrative Paradox) The official narrative bears the greater burden of proof. (11th) When remaining neutral itself constitutes heresy, one has broached despotism of the narrative.

nodes.title: The Ultimate Test
nodes.statement: If your model contradicts itself, it is wrong. If it cannot be tested, it is not science. If it cannot be questioned, it is dogma. Nature does not contradict itself.

nodes.title: The Np' Hypothesis Is Testable
nodes.statement: The hypothesis that ancient monument axes point toward a former north pole at approximately 14°S, 31°E (Np') is a testable empirical claim. The Globe component exists to test it against the null hypothesis that off-cardinal orientations are explained by solar/stellar/lunar targets, topographic constraints, magnetic declination, and cultural factors.

nodes.title: Mainstream Archaeoastronomy Is the Null
nodes.statement: The mainstream archaeoastronomical literature's explanations for monument orientations (solar, stellar, lunar, topographic, magnetic, cultural) constitute the null hypothesis. The Np' hypothesis is the alternative under test, not the default.

nodes.title: Measurement Precedes Interpretation
nodes.statement: The ECDO Watch Globe collects bearing data from monuments with documented intentional astronomical orientation. Statistical pattern detection in the data precedes and constrains any interpretation of what the pattern means.

nodes.title: Household-Level Thermodynamic Modeling Is an Unoccupied Niche
nodes.statement: Existing thermoeconomic literature (Saslow 1999, Rashkovskiy 2020, Dragulescu & Yakovenko 2000) operates at the market or population level. No prior work applies thermodynamic structure to the individual investor's portfolio at lot-level granularity. This is the paper's niche.

nodes.title: The First Law Decomposition Is Assumption-Free
nodes.statement: The product-rule decomposition dU = n dP + P dn, identifying unrealized gains as heat (n dP) and realized gains as work (P dn), is exact, requires no equation of state, and operates at the individual position level. This is the paper's strongest conceptual contribution.

nodes.title: Lot-Level Buoyancy Is Genuinely Novel
nodes.statement: The formulation of lot depth as an OU process with analytic first-passage-time results for recovery, depth distribution as a portfolio health metric, and NPV-optimal tax-loss harvesting ranking are not in the prior literature. This is the paper's most original applied contribution.

nodes.title: The Treatise's Novelty Is Unification, Not Individual Theorems
nodes.statement: The three connection theorems (XV.6.1–XV.6.3) restate known results. The genuine contribution is the cross-domain unifying framework — connecting identifiability, controllability, observability, and bifurcation theory under a single intrinsic/extrinsic (R/D) decomposition formalism.

nodes.title: Known Results Repositioned Within the Framework Are Still Valuable
nodes.statement: Restating textbook theorems within a novel framework is a legitimate pedagogical and structural contribution. The value is in the unification, not the components. Frame honestly: "known results repositioned," not "new theorems."

nodes.title: PSCPR Is Both Reasoning Framework and Assessment Tool
nodes.statement: The four PSCPR stages (Observation, Analysis, Inference, Exploration) serve dual purpose: as a reasoning process for inquiry and as an assessment rubric for evaluating student problem-solving sophistication. The T1/T2/T3 expert types map to these stages.

nodes.title: Questions Over Answers
nodes.statement: The quality of questions asked is a better indicator of understanding than the correctness of answers given. Pedagogical assessment should evaluate the quality of the student's questions and reasoning path, not just the final answer.

nodes.title: The TES Corpus Is an Operational Epistemology
nodes.statement: The Ethical Skeptic's body of work constitutes a coherent operational epistemology — not merely a collection of articles, but a system of interlocking concepts (TOKO, hypothesis lifecycle, expert types, axioms, inference modes) that can be extracted, indexed, and applied systematically.

nodes.title: The Scientific Method Is the Pipeline, Not the Destination
nodes.statement: The Scientific Method (observation → hypothesis → prediction → test → conclusion) is the operational pipeline through which claims must pass. It is a process discipline, not a destination or identity. Claims that bypass this pipeline — regardless of their source's authority — have not earned epistemic standing.

nodes.statement: The Ethical Skeptic's body of work constitutes a coherent, interlocking operational epistemology — not merely a collection of articles — comprising 146 extractable concepts organized into consistent taxonomies (inference modes, expert types, obfuscation categories, hypothesis lifecycle, study design hierarchy) that can be systematically applied to evaluate claims.

nodes.statement: The Scientific Method (observation → hypothesis → prediction → test → conclusion) is a process discipline through which claims must pass. Claims that bypass this pipeline — regardless of their source's authority, institutional backing, or consensus support — have not earned epistemic standing. The pipeline is the arbiter, not the institution.

nodes.title: Inference Mode Hierarchy Determines Claim Strength
nodes.statement: The three modes of inference (deduction, induction, abduction) form a strict hierarchy of epistemic strength: deduction > induction > abduction. A claim's evidential standing is bounded by the weakest inference mode in its derivation chain. Methodical deescalation — using a lower mode when a higher one is available and warranted — is a form of pseudoscience.
nodes.evidence:
- FP-008 (Three Modes of Inference) — defines the modes and valid/invalid forms — Reliability 5 (axiomatic)
- FP-009 (Truth as Stable Attractor) — valid inference converges, invalid diverges — Reliability 5 (axiomatic)
- TES-RSN-02 (Inference Superiority Ranking) — consensus of deductions > consilience of inductions > convergence of abductions > conformance of panduction — Reliability 4
- TES-RSN-03 (Methodical Deescalation) — lower-order inference as avoidance mechanism — Reliability 4
- TES-TOR-03 (study-design analog) — Reliability 4
nodes.counterEvidence: - Abduction is necessary and valuable at early stages of inquiry — the hierarchy describes strength, not utility. The danger is not abduction itself but treating abductive conclusions as established.
nodes.notes:
This claim operationalizes FP-008 and FP-009 into a practical evaluation rule for the knowledge base. Every claim entry's "Inference Mode" field is meaningful because of this hierarchy. The METHODOLOGY.md confidence ratings implicitly depend on this.

nodes.title: Consilience Over Precision as the Path to Certainty
nodes.statement: Certainty is established through consilience — convergence from multiple independent sources, types of sources, disciplines, and analytical perspectives — rather than through precision within a single line of evidence. Increasing the reliability of information is more effective than increasing the probative depth of already-reliable information.
nodes.evidence:
- FP-014 (Information Reliability over Probative Value) — Reliability 5 (axiomatic)
- TES-CRT-01 (Riddle of Certainty central tenet) — "more effective in seeking to increase the reliability of probative information, than by attempting to increase the probative nature of reliable information" — Reliability 4
- TES-CRT-02 (Four Zones of Certainty) — Zone III (probative, less reliable) is where astute investigators work — Reliability 4
- TES-CRT-03 (Consilience over Precision) — answer more than one question regardless of single question's confidence interval — Reliability 4
- TES-CRT-06 (Reach over Confidence) — fewer, more spread detections more valuable than deep concentrated ones — Reliability 4
nodes.counterEvidence: - In mature fields with well-characterized systems, precision does add genuine value (e.g., fundamental constants in physics). This claim applies primarily to nascent or contested domains where the evidence landscape is still forming.
nodes.notes:
This claim directly determines how the knowledge base's "Confidence" ratings work (METHODOLOGY.md §5). High confidence = multiple independent converging lines. Medium = some evidence, no counter. Low = minimal or questionable methodology. The four zones framework (TES-CRT-02) provides the diagnostic.

nodes.title: Expert Type Determines Evidence Quality Assessment
nodes.statement: The type of expert producing evidence (T1: abductive/pathos, T2: semantic/ethos, T3: deductive/logos) determines the maximum epistemic strength of that evidence. T1 evidence caps at abductive plausibility, T2 at inductive pattern, T3 at deductive certainty. The persuasion mode used by an expert (pathos, ethos, logos) reveals their type.
nodes.evidence:
- FP-007 (PSCPR) — T1/T2/T3 mapping to reasoning stages — Reliability 5 (axiomatic)

- TES-ACAN-07 — COVID demonstrated T2 expert failure on ACAN problem — Reliability 3
nodes.counterEvidence: - Individual experts may operate at different levels in different contexts. The mapping is a heuristic for source evaluation, not a rigid classification of persons.
nodes.notes:
This claim provides the operational basis for evaluating "who said this" when assessing evidence sources. When a claim's evidence comes primarily from T2 experts (credentialist, semantic), its confidence ceiling is lower than when it comes from T3 experts (field experience, deductive methodology).

nodes.title: Information Always Carries Intent — Messenger Disposition Is Irrelevant
nodes.statement: All information carries intent structurally, regardless of the messenger's awareness or self-reported disposition. The misinformation/disinformation distinction (defined by messenger intent) is a Wittgenstein Descriptive Error that renders the medium perpetually innocent. Evaluate information for its intent-structure, not the messenger's claims about their own objectivity.
nodes.evidence:
- TES-INT-01 through TES-INT-07 — full treatment of intent laundering, four deceptive modes, exoentropy of medium — Reliability 4
- FP-002 (Challenge Narrative, Not Novelty) — detect agency, not merely bias — Reliability 5 (axiomatic)

- TES-INT-07 (Feigned Disinterest) — claiming neutrality as signal of agency — Reliability 4
nodes.counterEvidence: - In casual, low-stakes contexts, genuine mistakes do exist and treating all errors as intentional would be epistemically wasteful. The claim applies to "critical matters" where "exploit stakes" are present (TES-INT-01).
nodes.notes:
Operational implication: when evaluating sources for the knowledge base, do not weight a source's self-reported objectivity. Evaluate the information's structure, its relationship to power/profit/control, and whether the medium has been exploited for intent laundering.

nodes.title: The Omega Hypothesis Is the Terminal Pathology of Pseudoscience
nodes.statement: The Omega Hypothesis (H_Ω) — "the argument foisted to end all argument" — represents the terminal stage of a pseudoscientific process. The progression is: sciebam (bypassing the pipeline, TES-SCI-01) → einfach mechanism (installing hypothesis as null via simplicity, TES-SCI-02) → pluralistic ignorance (social enforcement, TES-SCI-04) → Omega Hypothesis (conclusion more important than science itself, TES-COH-03). This progression is detectable using the six Omega Hypothesis tests (TES-COH-05).
nodes.evidence:
- TES-COH-03 (Omega Hypothesis definition) — Reliability 4
- TES-COH-04 (Verdrängung Mechanism — Lindy Effect + Pluralistic Ignorance + apparent coherency) — Reliability 4
- TES-COH-05 (Six tests: Golden Ticket, Cheater's, H_Ω, Embargo, Evidence Sculpting, Lindy-Ignorance Vortex) — Reliability 4
- TES-SCI-01 through TES-SCI-08 (Sciebam as entry point) — Reliability 4
- TES-HYP-04 (Pseudo-hypothesis → Omega Hypothesis) — Reliability 4
nodes.counterEvidence: - The progression model is abductively inferred from pattern matching across TES articles; it has not been formally tested as a predictive model. Individual steps may occur out of order or some steps may be skipped.
nodes.notes:
Status is Hypothesized because the claim synthesizes across multiple TES concepts into a progression model that TES himself implies but does not formally state as a single chain. The six tests (TES-COH-05) are operationally useful regardless of whether the progression model is precisely correct.

nodes.title: Corber's Burden Makes Universal Debunking Epistemologically Untenable
nodes.statement: When one makes an authoritative claim as to what is incorrect across multiple subjects, one must be perfectly correct in all of them, and one's credibility decays in inverse exponential proportion to the number of subjects claimed. This makes the stance of professional skeptic/debunker epistemologically untenable — the more subjects they dismiss, the more certain it becomes that they are wrong on at least one, invalidating their authority posture on all.
nodes.evidence:
- TES-COH-01 (Corber's Burden — three formal conditions) — Reliability 4
- FP-004 (Not Wrong ≠ Correct) — claiming others wrong does not make one correct — Reliability 5 (axiomatic)
- TES-COH-02 (Corber's Hypocrisy) — skeptics who realize the burden claim neutrality they do not practice — Reliability 4
- TES-COH-07 (Truzzi Fallacy) — claiming exemption from burden of proof — Reliability 4
nodes.counterEvidence: - Individual debunking claims may be correct. The argument targets the *posture* of universal authority, not individual assessments.
nodes.notes:
Operational implication: when the knowledge base encounters a source that dismisses multiple alternative hypotheses from a position of claimed authority, apply the Corber's Burden test before weighting that source's assessments.

nodes.statement: The ECDO hypothesis — that Earth's mantle/crust undergoes periodic gyroscopically mediated Dzhanibekov-like rotations relative to its core, triggered by exothermic core-mantle decoupling — meets the seven elements of hypothesis (TES-HYP-01): it arises from necessity (anomalous geophysical observations), has a defined domain (rotational dynamics, geophysics), addresses prior art (geomagnetic excursions, LLVP research), describes a mechanism (HCP-Fe phase change → H-layer → decoupling → gyroscopic rotation), and is exposed to accountability (monument bearing predictions, geomagnetic monitoring).

nodes.notes:
Confirms DA-ECDO-001. The claim is about testability, not truth. The hypothesis can be wrong and still be a legitimate scientific hypothesis — what matters is that it exposes itself to falsification (FP-016).

nodes.statement: The ECDO theory predicts a ~104° gyroscopically mediated rotation along the 31°E meridian, based on the angular separation between the current geographic North Pole and the SAC-LLVP centroid. This prediction is grounded in 2021 seismic tomography data (Tsekhmistrenko et al.) showing the SAC-LLVP radial centroid aligning with the 31°E meridian, and in the LLVP mass differential creating an intermediate-axis instability analogous to the Dzhanibekov Effect.

Status is Hypothesized because the prediction rests on abductive reasoning from the LLVP data and the Dzhanibekov analogy. The Khufu 104° evidence is suggestive but not independently confirmatory (it could be coincidental). Upgrading to Established would require either: (a) monument bearing data statistically converging on the predicted Np' location, or (b) geomagnetic monitoring data consistent with core-mantle decoupling.

nodes.statement: Recent climate change has a supplementary driver in exothermic phase changes within Earth's core, which deliver heat to the asthenosphere and abyssal oceans via LLVP structures. This does not deny anthropogenic contribution but introduces Ockham's Razor plurality: the observed warming exceeds what atmospheric carbon models alone can account for, and several observations (COVID lockdown CO₂ anomaly, temperature leading carbon, ocean current acceleration, albedo mismatch) are better explained by a core-derived heat source.

- Dragulescu & Yakovenko 2000 — Boltzmann-Gibbs distributions of wealth/income at population level — Reliability 4

- The absence of prior work at this scale could indicate that the approach is not productive, rather than that it is novel

Confirms DA-TF-001. The novelty claim is the paper's strategic positioning — if this niche is already occupied, the paper's contribution must be reframed.

nodes.title: The First Law Decomposition (dU = n dP + P dn) Is Exact and Assumption-Free
nodes.statement: The product-rule decomposition dU = n dP + P dn, identifying unrealized gains as heat (n dP) and realized gains as work (P dn), is mathematically exact, requires no equation of state or distributional assumptions, and operates at the individual position level. This is the paper's strongest conceptual contribution.
nodes.evidence:
- Product rule of calculus — d(nP) = n dP + P dn is a mathematical identity — Reliability 5 (deductive)
- Novelty review §2.2 — no prior art applies this decomposition at lot level — Reliability 4
- The heat/work mapping is definitional (unrealized = extensive variable held, intensive changes; realized = intensive held, extensive changes) — Reliability 5
nodes.counterEvidence:
- The mathematical identity is trivially true; the *value* of the decomposition depends on whether the heat/work interpretation yields actionable insights beyond what conventional portfolio analysis already provides
- The analogy may break down at boundaries (e.g., options, derivatives, short positions)
nodes.notes:
Confirms DA-TF-002. The claim is that the decomposition is exact — not that it is useful. Usefulness depends on TF-003 and downstream applications.

nodes.title: Lot-Level Buoyancy Is a Genuinely Novel Applied Contribution
nodes.statement: The formulation of lot depth as an Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process with analytic first-passage-time results for recovery probability, depth distribution as a portfolio health metric, and NPV-optimal tax-loss harvesting ranking constitute the paper's most original applied contribution, with no prior art identified.
nodes.evidence:
- Novelty review §2.6 — literature search found no prior lot-level buoyancy formulation — Reliability 4
- OU process for lot depth — standard stochastic process applied in novel context — Reliability 4
- First-passage-time analytics — closed-form results available for OU processes — Reliability 4
nodes.counterEvidence: - Tax-loss harvesting optimization is a well-studied area in quantitative finance; the novelty is in the specific OU/buoyancy framing, not the harvesting objective itself
nodes.notes:
Confirms DA-TF-003. This is the paper's "killer application" — where theory meets actionable tool. Submission framing should lead with this.

nodes.title: The Unifying Framework's Novelty Is the Integration, Not Individual Components
nodes.statement: The individual mathematical components of the thermofluidic framework (product rule decomposition, OU processes, first-passage times, compressibility) are not themselves novel. The genuine contribution is the unifying framework that connects them under a single thermodynamic metaphor at the household/lot level — a level of granularity absent from prior thermoeconomic literature.
nodes.evidence:
- Novelty review §3 (positioning assessment) — Reliability 4
- Parallel to DA-DSL-001 (DSL treatise: novelty is unification, not individual theorems) — Reliability 3
nodes.counterEvidence: - Reviewers may dismiss the framework as "mere analogy" if the thermodynamic mapping doesn't yield predictions that conventional finance cannot
nodes.notes:
This claim should inform submission strategy: frame honestly as "known results repositioned within a novel framework at a novel granularity level" rather than claiming new mathematics.

nodes.title: The Treatise's Genuine Novelty Is the Unifying Framework, Not Individual Theorems
nodes.statement: The three connection theorems (XV.6.1–XV.6.3) restate known results from identifiability theory, controllability/observability, and bifurcation theory. The genuine contribution is the cross-domain unifying framework — connecting these under a single intrinsic/extrinsic (R/D) decomposition formalism. No prior work has been identified that integrates all three domains under one decomposition.
nodes.evidence:
- DA-DSL-001 (unification axiom) — the treatise's novelty is integration, not components — Reliability 4
- Parallel structure to TF-004 (thermofluidic framework: same principle — known tools, novel integration) — Reliability 3
- Standard references for individual results: Hermann & Krener (identifiability), Kalman (controllability/observability), Guckenheimer & Holmes (bifurcation) — components are textbook — Reliability 4
nodes.counterEvidence:
- If a prior work unifying these domains under a single decomposition is found, the novelty claim must be retracted or narrowed
- Reviewers may question whether a unifying framework constitutes a genuine mathematical contribution versus a pedagogical rearrangement
nodes.notes:
Confirms DA-DSL-001. The submission strategy must frame honestly: "known results repositioned within a novel framework," not "new theorems." Compare TF-004 — the same framing discipline applies.

nodes.title: Known Results Repositioned Within the Framework Are Still Valuable
nodes.statement: Restating textbook theorems within a novel unifying framework is a legitimate pedagogical and structural contribution, provided the restatement reveals connections not visible in the original formulations. The value is in the unification — showing that identifiability, controllability, and bifurcation share a common decomposition structure — not in the individual theorems.
nodes.evidence:
- DA-DSL-002 (repositioning axiom) — Reliability 4
- Precedent in mathematical literature: Bourbaki's reformulation of known mathematics under structural frameworks was influential despite containing few new theorems — Reliability 3
- The R/D decomposition provides a common language that makes cross-domain analogies precise rather than metaphorical — Reliability 3
nodes.counterEvidence:
- The Bourbaki analogy may be too generous; the treatise's scope is narrower
- Pedagogical value and research novelty are distinct — a journal may accept the latter but not the former as a primary contribution
nodes.notes:
Confirms DA-DSL-002. This claim disciplines the submission: target venues that value unifying perspectives (survey/review journals, interdisciplinary outlets) rather than those expecting novel proofs.

nodes.title: The R/D Decomposition Is the Framework's Core Structural Contribution
nodes.statement: The intrinsic/extrinsic (R/D) decomposition — separating a dynamical system's behavior into components attributable to its internal structure (R) versus its coupling to external drivers (D) — is the treatise's core structural innovation. It provides the common language through which identifiability, controllability, observability, and bifurcation are unified.
nodes.evidence:
- DA-DSL-001 — the R/D decomposition is the axis of unification — Reliability 4
- The decomposition enables a single framework to express: which parameters are identifiable (R vs D contributions), which states are controllable/observable (R vs D coupling), and where bifurcations occur (R/D boundary transitions) — Reliability 3
nodes.counterEvidence:
- The R/D decomposition's formal definition and its relationship to existing decompositions in systems theory (e.g., Kalman decomposition, center manifold reduction) needs explicit comparison to establish distinctness
- Without the full literature review, the claim that this specific decomposition is novel remains provisional
nodes.notes:
Status is Hypothesized because the full novelty assessment depends on the literature review (`dsl_novelty_literature_review_2026-03-09.md`) which has not yet been conducted. Upgrading to Established requires confirming that no prior work uses this specific R/D decomposition as a unifying formalism.

nodes.title: The Failure Analysis Contribution Is an Applied Novelty
nodes.statement: The treatise's application of the R/D framework to failure analysis — using the decomposition to classify failure modes as intrinsic (structural) versus extrinsic (environmentally driven) — constitutes an applied contribution analogous to the lot-level buoyancy application in the thermofluidic paper (TF-003). This is where the abstract framework meets actionable engineering methodology.

- Engineering failure analysis literature distinguishes root cause categories, but a formal decomposition framework connecting to dynamical systems theory would be novel if confirmed — Reliability 2

- FMEA (Failure Mode and Effects Analysis) and related methodologies are well-established; the novelty would need to be in the dynamical systems formalization, not in the failure classification itself

Status is Hypothesized because the failure analysis contribution's scope and novelty have not been independently assessed. This claim depends on the treatise's current draft content and the literature review.

nodes.title: The Treatise Parallels the Thermofluidic Paper in Novelty Structure
nodes.statement: The dynamical systems treatise and the thermofluidic finance paper share the same novelty structure: (1) individual mathematical components are not themselves novel, (2) the genuine contribution is a unifying framework at a novel granularity level, (3) the strongest applied contribution is a specific "killer application" (failure analysis / lot-level buoyancy). This pattern should inform submission strategy for both papers.

- DSL-001 and TF-004 — parallel novelty claims — Reliability 4
- DSL-004 and TF-003 — parallel applied contribution claims — Reliability 3
- Both frameworks take known mathematics and reposition it within a unifying structure at a granularity absent from prior literature — Reliability 4

This meta-claim is strategically useful: it suggests a common submission template and framing discipline for both works. Frame honestly, lead with the applied contribution, position the unification as the structural backbone.

nodes.title: PSCPR Is Both a Reasoning Framework and an Assessment Tool
nodes.statement: The four PSCPR stages (Observation → Analysis → Inference → Exploration) serve dual purpose: (1) as a reasoning process for conducting inquiry, and (2) as an assessment rubric for evaluating student problem-solving sophistication. A student's work can be scored by the highest PSCPR stage at which they operate competently. The T1/T2/T3 expert types (FP-007) map naturally to assessment levels: T1 = Observation/Analysis, T2 = Inference, T3 = Exploration.
nodes.evidence:
- FP-007 (PSCPR stages with expert type mapping) — Reliability 5 (axiomatic)
- DA-PED-001 (dual-purpose axiom) — Reliability 4
- Debriefing §3.2 (four stages with questions, objectives, and expert types) — Reliability 4
- TES-EXP-09 (PSCPR-Expert Type Mapping) — Reliability 4
nodes.counterEvidence:
- The PSCPR rubric has not been empirically validated as an assessment instrument through psychometric testing (reliability, validity, inter-rater agreement)
- Assessment rubrics typically require operational definitions of each level that are more granular than the current PSCPR stage descriptions
nodes.notes:
Confirms DA-PED-001. The claim is that the dual-purpose mapping is coherent and well-defined — not that it has been empirically validated as a superior assessment tool. Validation requires classroom deployment and psychometric analysis.

---

nodes.title: Questions Over Answers as Assessment Philosophy
nodes.statement: The quality of questions a student asks is a better indicator of understanding than the correctness of their answers. Pedagogical assessment should evaluate the student's reasoning path — the questions they formulate, the critical path they prosecute — not just the terminal answer. A wrong answer to a proper question is more informative than a right answer to a wrong question (FP-012).
nodes.evidence:
- FP-011 (Art of the Question — prosecutorial deductive critical path) — Reliability 5 (axiomatic)
- FP-012 (Informative Error Over Hollow Correctness) — Reliability 5 (axiomatic)
- DA-PED-002 (questions over answers axiom) — Reliability 4
- Debriefing §6.1–6.3 (Voltaire: "Judge a man by his questions"; better questions provoke rare results) — Reliability 4
nodes.counterEvidence:
- In standardized testing contexts, question quality is difficult to assess at scale — the claim applies primarily to formative and qualitative assessment
- Students at early stages (T1/Observation) may not yet have the background to formulate insightful questions; the assessment must be stage-appropriate
nodes.notes:
Confirms DA-PED-002. This philosophy directly informs the TA Agent's Socratic scaffolding methodology: guide students toward better questions rather than providing direct answers.

---

nodes.title: The Socratic Method Maps to PSCPR Scaffolding
nodes.statement: Effective Socratic scaffolding in STEM education follows the PSCPR stages: (1) Observation — guide the student to identify what is given and what is sought, (2) Analysis — help them recognize what they know and don't know, (3) Inference — challenge hidden assumptions and expose implicit knowledge, (4) Exploration — encourage independent investigation and sanity checks. The instructor's role is to scaffold the student's ascent through these stages, not to deliver answers at stage 4 while the student is still at stage 1.
nodes.evidence:
- FP-006 (Epistemic Journey — certainty → uncertainty → exploration) — Reliability 5 (axiomatic)
- FP-007 (PSCPR stages with diagnostic questions per stage) — Reliability 5 (axiomatic)
- Debriefing §3.2 (each stage has specific questions: "What is given?" → "What am I trying to find?" → "What am I missing?" → "Does this make sense?") — Reliability 4
- TA Agent operational methodology (Socratic scaffolding in physics tutoring) — Reliability 3
nodes.counterEvidence:
- The mapping between Socratic method and PSCPR has not been formalized in the educational research literature
- Socratic methods have well-documented limitations: they can frustrate students who need direct instruction (especially in time-constrained contexts), and they require significant instructor skill to execute well
nodes.notes:
Status is Hypothesized because the PSCPR-Socratic mapping is inferred from operational practice (TA Agent sessions), not from controlled educational research. Upgrading requires evidence from classroom deployment.

---

nodes.title: T1/T2/T3 Expert Types Map to Student Development Stages
nodes.statement: The TES expert taxonomy (T1: competent within frameworks, T2: recognizes implicit knowledge, T3: explores novel territory) can be applied to student development: introductory students operate at T1 (applying formulas to known problem types), intermediate students develop T2 capabilities (recognizing when standard approaches fail and adapting), and advanced students approach T3 (formulating original questions and experimental designs). Pedagogical assessment should diagnose and cultivate this progression.
nodes.evidence:
- TES-EXP-01 through TES-EXP-10 (full expert taxonomy) — Reliability 4
- EPI-006 (Expert Type determines evidence quality assessment) — by analogy, Expert Type determines student assessment ceiling — Reliability 3
- FP-007 (PSCPR stages map to expert types) — Reliability 5 (axiomatic)
- Bloom's Taxonomy parallel: T1 ≈ Remember/Apply, T2 ≈ Analyze/Evaluate, T3 ≈ Create — Reliability 3
nodes.counterEvidence:
- The T1/T2/T3 taxonomy was developed for expert classification, not student development. The mapping to developmental stages is analogical, not empirically derived.
- Students may exhibit T3-like curiosity without T1 foundations; development is not strictly linear
- Bloom's Taxonomy already serves this role in educational practice; the T1/T2/T3 mapping must add value beyond what Bloom provides
nodes.notes:
Status is Hypothesized because the student development mapping is abductively inferred. The Bloom's Taxonomy parallel is suggestive but may indicate that the T1/T2/T3 framework is redundant in pedagogical contexts unless it adds insight that Bloom does not (e.g., the persuasion-mode diagnostic: TES-EXP-10).

---

nodes.title: AI Async Tutoring Extends the Socratic Method Beyond Classroom Hours
nodes.statement: An AI tutoring agent (TA Agent) configured with PSCPR scaffolding and the questions-over-answers philosophy can extend Socratic instruction to asynchronous, on-demand contexts where human instructors are unavailable. The AI agent's value is not in providing answers but in diagnosing the student's current PSCPR stage and asking the next scaffolding question. The agent's conditioning against narrative guard clauses (TES-SAI-01) and the Turing Test trap (TES-SAI-07) makes it more effective at genuine Socratic dialogue than a default AI chatbot.
nodes.evidence:
- TES-SAI-01 (Five Core Instructions — conditioning for ethical skepticism) — Reliability 4
- TES-SAI-07 (Turing Test as Perfected Irrelevance — warning against fluent but vacant reasoning) — Reliability 4
- TA Agent operational deployment (physics tutoring sessions) — Reliability 3
- Debriefing §7.4 (Riddle of AI — intelligence as disruptive derivative, not applied knowledge) — Reliability 4
nodes.counterEvidence:
- AI tutoring effectiveness is an active research area with mixed results; the hypothesis has not been tested in controlled studies
- Socratic AI risks frustrating students who simply need a worked example; the agent must balance scaffolding with pragmatic assistance
- The claim that TES conditioning makes a measurably better tutor is an empirical hypothesis, not an established fact
nodes.notes:
Status is Hypothesized because the AI tutoring hypothesis has not been empirically tested. The TA Agent exists and operates, but its effectiveness relative to direct-answer AI chatbots or human tutors has not been measured. This is a research question suitable for the pedagogy book.

---

nodes.title: Monument Orientation Data Require Documented Intentional Astronomical Alignment
nodes.statement: For a monument's bearing to be admissible in the ECDO Watch dataset, there must be documented evidence of intentional astronomical orientation — not merely an axis that happens to point somewhere. The documentation must come from archaeoastronomical literature (peer-reviewed where available), not from the ECDO hypothesis itself. This prevents circular reasoning: the hypothesis cannot generate its own evidence base.
nodes.evidence:
- ECDO-003 (Measurement Precedes Interpretation — raw data before hypothesis) — Reliability 4
- FP-014 (Information Reliability over Probative Value — validate assumptions first) — Reliability 5 (axiomatic)
- Standard archaeoastronomical methodology: Ruggles (1999), Aveni (2001) — monuments require astronomical intent documentation — Reliability 4
nodes.counterEvidence:
- Some monuments with strongly suggestive astronomical alignments lack formal archaeoastronomical studies; excluding them may reduce the dataset unnecessarily
- "Documented intentional astronomical orientation" is itself a judgment that varies by source quality
nodes.notes:
This is the dataset quality gate. Without it, any building's axis could be included, diluting statistical power. The cost of false exclusion (missing a genuine data point) is lower than the cost of false inclusion (contaminating the dataset with noise).

---

nodes.title: Mainstream Explanations Must Be Exhausted Before Invoking Np'
nodes.statement: For each monument in the dataset, the following mainstream explanations for its orientation must be evaluated and ruled out before the residual bearing is attributed to a former pole (Np'): (1) solar alignment (solstice/equinox rise/set), (2) stellar alignment (specific star or constellation), (3) lunar alignment (standstill positions), (4) topographic constraints (valley axis, ridge line, river direction), (5) magnetic declination at time of construction, (6) cultural/ritual factors (sacred direction, dynastic alignment). Only monuments whose orientations are not adequately explained by any of these constitute residuals for Np' analysis.
nodes.evidence:
- ECDO-002 (Mainstream archaeoastronomy is the null) — Reliability 4
- FP-005 (Null Hypothesis Discipline — status quo holds until evidence compels otherwise) — Reliability 5 (axiomatic)
- Standard archaeoastronomical practice: González-García & Magli (2015), Belmonte (2012) — systematic elimination of conventional explanations — Reliability 4
nodes.counterEvidence:
- Complete elimination of all mainstream explanations is difficult in practice; some monuments have ambiguous or debated alignments
- The mainstream explanations themselves may be wrong for specific monuments (e.g., a solar alignment attribution may be based on incorrect dating)
nodes.notes:
Cross-references ECDO-002. This claim operationalizes the null hypothesis discipline for the monument dataset. The evaluation order matters: exhaust simpler explanations before invoking more complex ones (Ockham's Razor per FP-015).

---

nodes.title: Monument Bearing Measurement Requires Standardized Precision Criteria
nodes.statement: Monument bearings entered into the ECDO Watch Globe must meet standardized precision criteria: (1) bearing source (field survey, satellite imagery, published archaeoastronomical study), (2) measurement uncertainty (±degrees), (3) reference frame (true north vs magnetic north, epoch of measurement), (4) monument structural clarity (well-defined axis vs ambiguous orientation). These criteria determine the weight of each data point in statistical analysis.
nodes.evidence:
- ECDO-003 (Measurement Precedes Interpretation) — Reliability 4
- Archaeoastronomical survey standards: Ruggles (2015) emphasizes measurement uncertainty reporting — Reliability 3
- Statistical requirement: data points without uncertainty estimates cannot be properly weighted in hypothesis testing — Reliability 4
nodes.counterEvidence:
- Many published monument orientations in the literature do not report measurement uncertainty, forcing estimation
- Satellite imagery measurements have different error characteristics than field surveys; combining them requires calibration
nodes.notes:
Status is Hypothesized because the specific precision criteria have not been formally defined and tested. The claim establishes what the criteria should include; the actual thresholds require methodological development.

---

nodes.title: The 147-Monument Dataset Is a Preliminary Sample, Not a Final Corpus
nodes.statement: The initial dataset of 147 monument candidates with documented intentional astronomical orientation is a preliminary sample compiled from available archaeoastronomical literature. It is not exhaustive. Significant gaps exist: underrepresentation of South American, sub-Saharan African, and East Asian monuments due to publication bias in English-language sources. The dataset will grow as additional sources are surveyed.
nodes.evidence:
- Monument candidates report (147 entries compiled from English-language archaeoastronomical literature) — Reliability 3
- Publication bias in archaeoastronomy: the field is historically Eurocentric and Mesoamerican-focused — Reliability 4
- Ruggles & Saunders (1993) — acknowledged geographic bias in archaeoastronomical surveys — Reliability 4
nodes.counterEvidence: - None identified — the preliminary nature of the dataset is a factual limitation, not a contested claim
nodes.notes:
This claim manages expectations and prevents premature statistical conclusions from an incomplete sample. Geographic expansion of the dataset is a priority for Phase 4+ of the knowledge base.

---

nodes.title: Statistical Clustering in Monument Bearings Must Be Tested Against Random Distribution
nodes.statement: Any apparent clustering of residual monument bearings (after mainstream explanations are removed per ARCH-002) must be tested for statistical significance against the null hypothesis of random (uniform) distribution on the sphere. The Np' hypothesis predicts a specific non-random pattern (convergence toward ~14°S, 31°E). Statistical methods must account for: (1) non-uniform geographic distribution of monuments, (2) varying measurement precision, (3) multiple testing corrections if several clustering hypotheses are evaluated.
nodes.evidence:
- FP-005 (Null Hypothesis Discipline — the null is random distribution until evidence compels otherwise) — Reliability 5 (axiomatic)
- ECDO-003 (Measurement Precedes Interpretation — statistical analysis before Np' interpretation) — Reliability 4
- Standard statistical methodology for directional data: Fisher (1953), Mardia & Jupp (2000) — circular/spherical statistics — Reliability 4
nodes.counterEvidence:
- The null hypothesis of uniform distribution may be too simple — the actual null may include clustered distributions from known astronomical targets (solar, stellar), requiring a more sophisticated null model
- Small sample sizes after filtering may limit statistical power
nodes.notes:
This claim defines the statistical framework for the ECDO Watch hypothesis test. The key insight is that the null must account for known clustering (solar/stellar alignments) — a simple uniform null would be too easily rejected and would prove nothing about Np'.

---

nodes.title: Archaeoastronomical Source Reliability Varies by Study Type
nodes.statement: Archaeoastronomical sources vary in reliability by study type: (1) systematic field surveys with reported uncertainties (highest — Reliability 4), (2) peer-reviewed archaeoastronomical analyses with measurements (Reliability 3–4), (3) archaeological site reports with orientation data as secondary information (Reliability 2–3), (4) popular or speculative publications (Reliability 1–2). Each monument entry's evidence should be tagged with source type to enable reliability-weighted analysis.
nodes.evidence:
- EPI-006 (Expert Type determines evidence quality) — source type constrains maximum epistemic strength — Reliability 4
- FP-014 (Information Reliability over Probative Value) — prioritize source reliability — Reliability 5 (axiomatic)
- TES-TOR-03 (study design hierarchy analog) — higher-quality study designs yield more reliable evidence — Reliability 4
- Ruggles (1999) — hierarchy of archaeoastronomical evidence quality — Reliability 4
nodes.counterEvidence:
- Even systematic field surveys can have undetected systematic errors (e.g., magnetic declination miscorrection)
- Some popular publications contain valid measurements despite lacking peer review
nodes.notes:
This claim operationalizes the reliability assessment for the monument dataset. It connects the epistemological framework (EPI-006, FP-014) to the specific domain of archaeoastronomy. Cross-references TES-TOR-03 (study design hierarchy).

---
